input.brief: Ohio one-person software studio: custom business software for non-technical small-business owners on one monthly subscription, built one layer at a time

direction.name: Colour chapters
direction.idea: Every section is a chapter with its own flat colour, floor to ceiling. The page reads like a set of posters hung in a row, held together by one typeface and one grid. The colours are not decoration: they come from the subject (the brand's packaging, the artist's record sleeves, the product's own colour ways, the categories of the content) and each chapter's colour means that chapter. Decide the sequence like a designer orders a book: a strong opener, a quiet second, a surprise in the middle, a dark or very light closer.
direction.composition: Sections are full-bleed fields, each at least 90svh tall, butted directly against each other with no gap and no divider. Inside every field the same 12-column grid and the same margins apply, and each field holds one thing: a huge heading (8–12vw) with a small paragraph, or one photograph with a caption, or one list. Text colour is chosen per field for strong contrast (ink or paper, never grey). Headings start on the same left edge in every chapter, so the eye feels the system as colours change. The navigation and the footer take the colours of the first and last chapter.
direction.typography: One typeface in two weights. Headings very large and tight; body 18–20px. Because colour is loud, the type stays plain: no italics, no second face.
direction.colour: Four to six flat fields used at full strength, one per section, each with its assigned text colour. No tints, no gradients between them: the hard edge where two fields meet is the look.
direction.imagery: Sparing. One photograph or object per chapter at most, either cut out and sitting directly on the colour, or a plain rectangle with generous colour around it. Photographs should be simple enough not to fight the field.
direction.richness: Colour at scale. A whole screen of one saturated colour is rich on its own, so a chapter needs few elements; it still needs its content at full size, because a coloured screen with one small line on it reads as empty.
direction.pitfalls: Check contrast on every field with the palette's assigned ink. Do not put cards on the fields. Do not use more than six colours. Two neighbouring fields should differ clearly in lightness as well as hue.

hero.name: Giant cropped shape
hero.blueprint: A plain ground with one flat shape at enormous scale. The shape is the simplest geometry found in the subject (a circle, a ring segment, a chamfered block, an arch), drawn in CSS or as a single inline SVG path and filled with the accent colour. It is about 120vh across and enters from the right, centred near 78% of the width and 55% of the height, so the top, right and bottom edges of the viewport crop it and its left boundary reaches column 7. If the subject has a true pair (two accounts, two modes), a second shape in a second flat colour overlaps the first by a quarter with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`. The headline sits on the bare ground on columns 1–6, vertically centred, flush left at 8% from the left edge: two lines at clamp(64px, 6.4vw, 100px), heavy weight, tracking -0.03em. Beneath it comes one supporting sentence at 19px, then the single action as a solid button cut to the same shape. A bold wordmark sits top-left at 32px; up to three text links sit top-right in the ground colour.
hero.mobile: The shape moves to the bottom: 130vw across, centred horizontally, its top at 56svh, cropped by the left, right and bottom edges. The headline sits above it at 11.5vw on two lines at a 16px margin, starting 15% down, with the sentence at 16px and the motif-shaped button beneath. Wordmark top-left; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: Two lines of two or three words each, up to about 12 characters per line at 6.4vw.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Staircase statement
sections.blueprint: On a flat dark or saturated field one sentence of 12–18 words is broken into five short lines at clamp(36px, 4.4vw, 64px), bold, leading 1.02, marked up as one paragraph (a statement, so it may run past two lines at this size). Each line starts further right than the one above: indents of 0, 6, 12, 18 and 24vw from a 4vw left margin, set with `padding-left` per line, so the block descends like stairs and ends near the 75% mark. Each line takes its own flat colour from the palette, or lines alternate between two inks. The block is vertically centred in a section 100svh tall. The right quarter (columns 10–12) holds two stacked photographs, each 3:2 and 20vw wide with a 16px gap, top-aligned with the first line. No heading; a two-line note at 15px sits at the bottom-left margin, on the first line's left edge. On a page without images, leave the right quarter empty.
sections.mobile: Five lines at 9vw (35px on a 390px screen) with indents of 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20vw, so the stair still reads on a 390px screen. The two photographs follow below as one row of two equal 3:2 frames. The note sits last, left-aligned.

sections.name: Accordion of tinted panels
sections.blueprint: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion. Introduction: the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), in columns 1–5; one paragraph at 18px in columns 7–11. 64px below, a flex row across columns 1–12, 520px tall, of four to six panels with no gaps. The open stage is a panel taking about 58% of the width; the rest are vertical slivers sharing what remains. Order is carried by colour: the first stage is the darkest tone of one hue and each later stage is a lighter flat tint of it, so the row reads dark to light from left to right. A sliver shows only its stage name, rotated 90 degrees and reading upward, at 20px bold, anchored to its bottom-left. The open panel shows the name at 40px top-left, a 36ch paragraph at 18px bottom-left and, optionally, one photograph in its right half. Clicking a sliver opens it (flex-basis transition, 450ms).
sections.mobile: The accordion turns vertical: stages stack at full width as bars 64px tall in the same dark-to-light order, names set horizontally at 18px. The open stage expands to its content height with the paragraph at 17px. The first stage is open by default.

sections.name: Names as one paragraph
sections.blueprint: All project or client names run together as one paragraph at poster scale: 10–18 names at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 78px), leading 1.1, flowing inline across the full width between 24px margins and wrapping where they fall, five to seven lines in all. Names are separated by a comma, or by a small inline frame: an `inline-block` 0.8em tall and 1.2em wide, aligned to the cap height, holding that project's photograph and placed directly after its name. Every name is a link; all names rest in the soft ink, and the hovered one takes full ink while its inline frame scales to 1.6 times from its left edge. A heading of two words opens the paragraph as its first words in full ink, on the same line and at the same size, followed by a colon. Below the paragraph at the left margin, one line at 15px gives the count and the years covered.
sections.mobile: The paragraph is set at 9vw, left-aligned, about twelve lines, with names separated by commas. Inline frames are removed except after the first three names, where they stay at cap height. All names are full ink; each remains a link with 6px of extra line spacing for touch.

sections.name: The ticket
sections.blueprint: The price is printed on a ticket. On a flat contrasting ground, one filled panel about 64vw wide with 2.3:1 proportions sits centred and straight, built as a two-part grid (7fr 3fr). A half-round notch 28px across is bitten out of the top and bottom edges where the two parts meet (two absolutely positioned circles in the ground colour), and a column of round dots 6px across in the ground colour runs between the notches as the perforation. The main part holds, top-left with 40px padding, what is being bought in two to four words at about 4vw, and along its bottom three or four short lines at 17px (dates, what is included, terms) in two tidy columns. The stub holds the price at about 6vw, centred, and under it the action as a solid bar the full width of the stub, 56px tall.
sections.mobile: The ticket turns upright: full width less 20px margins, main part on top, stub beneath, the notches now on the left and right edges and the dot perforation running across. Title at 9vw, price at 16vw, the action bar full width inside the stub.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Paul Kalkbrenner
references.idea: Swiss poster typography for a techno artist: the name as one black line with a photo set inside it like a glyph, then every chapter gets its own flat colour and visible grid.
references.hero: Pure white viewport. The artist's name sits on one line at exact vertical centre in bold black neo-grotesk, about 10.4vw, spanning roughly 78% of the width with equal side margins. The space between first and last name is replaced by a small landscape black-and-white photo, x-height tall and resting on the baseline. Top-left is a tiny circular monogram; eight nav links in 13px bold are spread at even intervals across the right half of the top edge. Bottom edge: equaliser bars with a grey label over a track title at left, a three-line bold blurb starting just left of centre, a sound toggle hard right. About 85% is empty.
references.type: ABC Diatype Plus Variable only: bold at -0.05em tracking for display and 13.5px bold for everything functional. Display runs from 150px in the hero to about 44vw elsewhere per the digest. Tiny uppercase labels inside boxed cells; no second face, no italics.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #c5c5c5 #a7ff9c #ff6831 — Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange. Photos inside coloured sections are tinted to the section hue or kept black-and-white.
references.imagery: Portraits and live shots of the artist: full-bleed colour images between sections, a grainy monochrome portrait marked up as a vinyl disc, a green duotone car portrait, and a strip of small mixed-ratio thumbnails. Square corners throughout.
references.layout: Outer margins of only 4-8px; content hangs on a visible column grid with hairlines and boxed cells. Sections alternate between full-bleed photographs and flat colour fields, each arranged differently, so the rhythm is one poster after another.

sections.description: Two words stacked in bold grotesk at roughly 8vw, each preceded by a solid black circle about the height of the lowercase, the second line indented further right than the first. Thin horizontal and vertical hairlines cross the white field at baselines and column edges like a construction grid. Directly beneath is a single row of streaming-service logos spaced evenly edge to edge, then a full-bleed photograph.

Flat mid-grey field split in two. Left half: a square grainy monochrome portrait with a large thin circle drawn on it and a small grey dot at the centre, so the photo reads as a record. Right half: a row of three year tabs and a small link above a hairline, the album title in small bold caps, a short description lower down, and along the bottom two wide outlined cells side by side acting as buttons.

Acid-mint field introducing the tour list. A large photograph, recoloured as a green-and-black duotone, occupies only the top-right quadrant; the left half is left empty. Along the bottom a table header with three tiny uppercase column labels sits on a hairline spanning the full width, where the list of dates begins.

Orange field. A horizontally scrolling strip of small photographs of differing widths runs across the top, cropped by both edges. Below it one outlined rectangle spans the width, divided into three equal cells: two inputs and a submit action, each identified only by tiny centred uppercase text. Small-print lines sit under the left and right cells.

steal: Replace the space between the two words of a giant name with a small photo cropped to x-height.
Flood each chapter with one flat colour and tint its photograph to match as a duotone.
Build forms and button pairs as adjoining outlined cells with tiny uppercase labels instead of filled buttons.

references.name: Warm & Fuzzy
references.idea: A showreel-first studio site in which every section takes one flat, loud colour (blue, black, yellow) under heavy grotesk type and a chunky custom wordmark.
references.hero: The showreel plays full-bleed with a visible film-grain overlay and no scrim. A chunky hand-cut wordmark sits top left, 16px from the edges; the same top line continues with a one-sentence status link, a tiny thumbnail beside the latest project's name, and three caps links at the far right, all white over the footage. A small green caps play label floats at dead centre. The tagline is anchored bottom left, 16px from both edges, in white grotesk caps at 47px (3.3vw) on one line spanning 56% of the width. A tiny square pause control sits bottom right.
references.type: SuisseIntl throughout, rendering heavy, tracked -0.027em: a 47px caps tagline, a caps section title at 9.4vw, statement paragraphs around 5vw with tight leading, and 10 to 11px caps captions. The logo is custom chunky lettering with wobbly cut-paper counters.
references.colour: #000000 #190bb6 #f7dd47 #ffffff #e9479f #1fc27a — Each section is a flat field: ultramarine blue, black, yellow, then blue again. White type on blue and black, black on yellow; a green play label is the only small accent.
references.imagery: Commercial stills and video (candy-coloured CG worlds, product renders, live-action frames) in square-cornered thumbnails of mixed aspect ratios, with a grain layer over the whole page and floating glossy 3D sticker objects.
references.layout: Tight 16px outer margins and edge-to-edge type. Sections are told apart by background colour rather than spacing: a blue statement set in the right two-thirds, a black packed work wall, a yellow full-width paragraph, a blue footer.

sections.description: On black, a tiny caps motto sits top left, then a caps section title at about 9vw flush left with a small underlined link at the far right on its baseline. Beneath, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall: widths vary from one-sixth to one-half of the page, heights differ, gaps are about 8px and rows do not align. Under each image a 10px caps line gives the project name left and the year in grey right.

A yellow field filled edge to edge by one paragraph in black heavy grotesk at roughly 5vw with very tight leading, left-aligned at the 16px margin. Several lines contain deliberate word-sized gaps, as if the text flowed around something, and a small tilted image chip floats over the first lines, covering parts of words.

A full-screen blue field. A top row of tiny caps, email left and three links right, sits above a hairline. A glossy 3D sticker object hangs near the top centre. The chunky wordmark runs the full page width at the bottom in white, about a fifth of the viewport tall, above a bar of tiny caps links divided by vertical hairlines.

steal: Give every section one flat saturated background and change it at each section break, keeping type strictly black or white.
Pack work thumbnails at mixed widths and heights with 8px gaps and a two-part micro caption (name left, year right) under each.
End with the wordmark at full page width on a colour field, with all utility links reduced to a tiny caps bar split by vertical hairlines.

references.name: wild
references.idea: A studio essay on craft versus AI in which everything decorative is drawn on one square-pixel grid: the hero heatmap, the icons, the diagrams, the marquee lettering and the footer equaliser.
references.hero: White page with a barely visible graph-paper grid. The top 22% is a masthead band split by a vertical hairline at 60%: at left, a two-line uppercase headline in a light grotesk at 5.2vw, tight leading, starting 9% from the left and nearly touching the top edge; at right, a two-line uppercase tagline with words spread to justify the column, then a pixel logo and a small right-aligned description. Below, a full-bleed canvas about 45% of the viewport tall: thousands of small squares in yellow, red, lime, cobalt and navy form a heatmap that erodes into white along its lower edge. A 3vw intro paragraph begins at the fold.
references.type: Sneak in one regular-to-light weight does everything: uppercase 75px headline at -0.035em, a 44px sentence-case intro, section headings near 30px, 13px body. Tiny SF Mono uppercase captions with wide tracking sit under headings. A bitmap pixel face appears once, in the closing marquee. No bold anywhere.
references.colour: #ffffff #0a0a0a #f2b90f #3b55d9 #1e2340 #e8452c — White page, black type, black buttons. Colour lives only inside the pixel graphics, in a fixed set of yellow, cobalt, navy, red and lime, so every illustration looks related. No section changes background.
references.imagery: Canvas-drawn square-pixel fields: a heatmap band, particle streams that tighten from scattered dots into a dense ribbon, pixel smiley faces, an equaliser strip. Client work appears once, as three plain square-cornered photo cards.
references.layout: Content runs from 9% to 91% with a constant split: heading in the left third, body in the right two-thirds, a tiny mono caption under the heading. Full-bleed pixel canvases interrupt the text. A small fixed mono link sits top-right; the ending is centred.

sections.description: Three equal cards in one row, each a 6:5 image with square corners (laptop mock-up, product photo, flat illustration) followed by a centred project name at about 20px and a centred two-line description in small text. No borders, shadows or tags; a small round black arrow button overlaps the right edge of the third image to advance the row. Large white space above and below.

Essay rows: a two- or three-line heading at about 2.2vw in the left third with a tiny wide-tracked mono caption below it; in the right two-thirds, two short justified paragraphs at 13px. Under one row, two pixel-art faces built from black squares (a smile and a frown, about 30px) sit side by side, each over a mono label and a three-line centred caption, forming a two-column comparison.

A four-word heading on two lines and a short paragraph at the left, then a wide canvas diagram: scattered pale-blue and navy squares at the left converge into a tight horizontal ribbon in the middle and fan out again in yellow at the right, a pixel funnel. Below it four narrow columns, each with a small round dark marker, a bold one-word label and two lines of small text.

A single line of bitmap lettering scrolls across the full width, each glyph assembled from yellow squares flecked with red, navy and lime. Centred beneath: a black button with stepped pixel corners, two short grey centred paragraphs and an email line. The page ends with a full-width strip of coloured pixel bars like an audio equaliser, a small black play button centred above it.

steal: Pick one drawing primitive, a square on a fixed grid, and render every non-text element with it (hero art, icons, diagrams, display lettering, footer) in one five-colour set.
Split a masthead band 60/40 with a vertical hairline: oversized light-weight uppercase headline at left, a word-spaced justified tagline and tiny descriptor at right.
Lay out long copy as rows with the heading in the left third and body in the right two-thirds, and put the tiny mono caption under each heading instead of an eyebrow above it.
